Spongionella gracilins and tetrahydroapsulphurin inhibit Ca2+-in fluxes through SOC channels by a mechanism involving the inhibition of mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP).
Spongionella secondary metabolites modulate store operated calcium entry by regulating mitochondrial functioning in human SH-SY5y neuroblastoma cells.
Spongionella gracilins A, L, and tetrahydro-aplysulphurinin-1 are new modulators of mitochondrial function and store operated calcium channels in neuroblastoma cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new natural products with potential therapeutic applications.
the study of the effect of four secondary products isolated from sponge Sponionella, gracilin H, A, and L and tetrahydroadiplysin-1 in the calcium ion (Ca2+)-fluxes of the neuroblastoma SH-SY5 cells.
the study of secondary metabolites isolated and purified from marine organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of Spongionella secondary metabolites on Ca2+ fluxes in SH-SY-5Y cells are due to the ability of these compounds to modulate mitochondrial functioning.
Spongionella gracilin A, L and Tetrahydroaplysulfurin-1 are new compounds able to modulate mitochondrial activity, which is the basis of the observed effects on calcium homeostasis in SH-SY-5Y cells.
Spongionella metabolites regulate SOC channels activity by a mechanism that involves mitochondrial functioning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the compounds isolated from sponge Sponionella modulate Ca2+ fluxes through SOC channels and mPTP by acting on mitochondria.
Spongionella gracilins and tetrahydro aplysulphurine-1 are able to inhibit Ca2+ entry through SOC channels by a mechanism that involves mitochondrial activity.

Spongionella gracilin A, L, and tetrahydro aplysulphurine-1 are able to inhibit Ca2+ influx in SH-SY 5Y neuroblastom cells by blocking the opening of mPTP, and that this effect is mediated by their ability to bind to Cyp D, a protein that is involved in mPTP opening.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Spongionella gracilin A, B, L and tetrahidroaplysulphorin-1 are potent mPTP blockers, a novel mechanism of action for this family of compounds.
the compounds we have studied have an effect on mitochondrial functioning.
